title: Collibra UI capability catalog
implementation_boundary: This is a framework-neutral contract. Consumer products own the runtime implementation and must keep it aligned with this catalog.

layout_policy.responsive_behavior: consumer-owned layout tokens; preserve hierarchy, task actions, and readable content at every supported viewport

token_policy.spacing: brand.space.scale is OPEN. Do not create a numeric spacing scale or place numeric spacing values in a component implementation here.
token_policy.status: Consumer products must provide semantic status tokens with contrast evidence. Do not infer warning or error colors from an unapproved ramp.
token_policy.icons: Consumer products may supply an icon set, but icon meaning never stands alone when text or accessible naming is required.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: Starts a clear action with an explicit verb and a predictable completion state.
components.keyboard: Focusable with Tab; activates with Enter or Space; keeps focus visible while loading and after completion.
components.semantics: Use a native button for an in-place action. Do not use a button to navigate to a URL.
components.accessibility: Accessible name is the visible action label; disabled and busy states are programmatically exposed; status changes do not rely on color alone.
content: Lead with a verb.
Keep one primary action per context.
Name the result when it matters, such as Save changes.
do: Keep the label stable while an action is in progress.
Make destructive intent explicit before the action.
avoid: Icon-only labels without an accessible name.
Using low-contrast ramp colors for text or controls.

components.name: Icon button
components.purpose: Provides a compact action when the icon has a familiar, unambiguous meaning and space is constrained.
components.keyboard: Focusable with Tab; activates with Enter or Space; tooltip is supplemental and never the only accessible name.
components.semantics: Use a button with an accessible name that describes the action, not the icon shape.
components.accessibility: Expose the accessible name in the control; provide a visible label or tooltip when the action is not universally understood.
content: Use action language such as Open filters or Copy link.
Keep the accessible name stable.
do: Use for repeated, space-constrained actions.
Keep destructive actions visually and verbally distinct.
avoid: Using a generic More label when the menu contents are unknown.
Using an icon as a status indicator without text or a programmatic announcement.

components.name: Link
components.purpose: Navigates to another location or resource while preserving normal browser and assistive technology expectations.
components.keyboard: Focusable with Tab and activates with Enter; preserves expected browser link behavior.
components.semantics: Use a native link for navigation. The destination or outcome is clear from the label or its accessible context.
components.accessibility: Do not communicate link meaning by color alone; distinguish visited or unavailable states with text or semantics where needed.
content: Name the destination or outcome.
Avoid vague labels such as Click here.
do: Use links for navigation and references.
Open a new context only when the label explains it.
avoid: Styling an in-place action as a link without a navigation outcome.
Removing native focus behavior.

components.name: Menu
components.purpose: Groups related, infrequent actions behind a labeled trigger without hiding the primary task path.
components.keyboard: Trigger opens with Enter or Space; Arrow keys move through items; Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger; type-ahead is supported when the menu is long.
components.semantics: Use menu semantics only for a list of actions. Use navigation semantics for a list of destinations.
components.accessibility: Expose the expanded state, item names, disabled state, and current item; keep focus inside the open menu until it closes.
content: Order items by task frequency and risk.
Use separators only when they communicate a meaningful group.
do: Keep the trigger label or accessible name stable.
Place destructive actions behind explicit labels and, when needed, confirmation.
avoid: Putting the primary action only in a menu.
Nested menus when a dedicated surface is clearer.

components.name: Text field
components.purpose: Collects a short, bounded value with a visible label, useful hint, and recoverable validation.
components.keyboard: Focusable with Tab; supports native text editing; validation does not trap focus or erase the user's input.
components.semantics: Use a native input or textarea with an associated label, description, and error relationship.
components.accessibility: Expose required, invalid, read-only, disabled, and described-by relationships; announce validation without relying on color alone.
content: Labels identify the value, not the format.
Hints explain constraints before entry.
Errors state what happened and how to fix it.
do: Validate at the point that helps the user recover.
Preserve entered values after an error.
avoid: Placeholder text as the only label.
Clearing a field on failed submit.

components.name: Combobox
components.purpose: Supports selection from a known set while allowing search or filtering when the set is large.
components.keyboard: Typing filters options; Arrow keys move through options; Enter selects; Escape closes without losing the query; Home and End work for long lists.
components.semantics: Use a combobox pattern only when the input and popup list have a clear relationship; otherwise use a select or search field.
components.accessibility: Expose expanded state, active option, list size when available, selected value, and no-results status.
content: Tell users whether they can create a new value.
Use a useful no-results message with a recovery path.
do: Keep the current query visible.
Make selection and filtering behavior predictable.
avoid: A popup that changes position without preserving active context.
Loading forever without a recovery message.

components.name: Checkbox
components.purpose: Captures one or more independent yes/no choices, including an optional indeterminate parent state.
components.keyboard: Focusable with Tab; toggles with Space; preserves the native checkbox interaction model.
components.semantics: Use a checkbox for independent choices, not for mutually exclusive selection or immediate mode changes.
components.accessibility: Associate the label and group description; expose checked, mixed, required, disabled, and invalid states.
content: Label the choice as a statement or setting.
Explain consequences when the choice changes behavior.
do: Use a group label when several choices share a context.
Preserve mixed state meaning in tree or bulk-selection contexts.
avoid: Making the entire row ambiguous about what is selected.
Using a checkbox for an immediate action with side effects.

components.name: Radio group
components.purpose: Captures exactly one choice from a small, visible set.
components.keyboard: Tab enters the group; Arrow keys move between options and update the selection; Space selects the focused option.
components.semantics: Use a radio group for mutually exclusive choices that should be compared together.
components.accessibility: Expose group name, option name, selected state, required state, and validation relationship.
content: Put the question in the group label.
Make each option distinct and comparable.
do: Use a select when the option set is long.
Keep the selected choice visible after navigation.
avoid: Allowing multiple options to be selected.
Hiding the group label in visual-only text.

components.name: Switch
components.purpose: Toggles a setting that takes effect immediately or clearly communicates when it will take effect.
components.keyboard: Focusable with Tab; toggles with Space; exposes pending state without becoming unresponsive.
components.semantics: Use a switch for an immediate setting change, not for a form submission or a choice requiring comparison.
components.accessibility: Expose checked state, accessible name, pending state, and any consequence that requires confirmation.
content: Label the setting, not the words On and Off alone.
Explain the effect when it is not obvious.
do: Keep state and outcome synchronized.
Offer an undo or recovery path for risky reversible changes.
avoid: Using a switch for a destructive or irreversible action.
Changing state without communicating failure.

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: Adds compact, secondary metadata such as status, type, or count without becoming the only source of meaning.
components.keyboard: Not interactive. If the badge becomes actionable, use a labeled button or link instead.
components.semantics: Expose meaningful text in the accessibility tree; decorative shape and color are supplementary.
components.accessibility: Never encode status with color alone; counts and status names remain available as text.
content: Use short, stable labels.
Prefer a meaningful status word over an unexplained color dot.
do: Use as supporting metadata next to a primary label.
Truncate only when the full value is available on demand.
avoid: Using badges as buttons without action semantics.
Using many competing badges in one row.

components.name: Alert
components.purpose: Communicates important information, validation, or recovery guidance in the current context.
components.keyboard: If dismissible, the dismiss control is focusable and returns focus to a sensible context; status announcements do not steal focus unexpectedly.
components.semantics: Use a status or alert role according to urgency; use a live region only when the user must be notified without moving focus.
components.accessibility: Expose severity and recovery instructions in text; do not rely on icon or color alone.
content: State what happened.
State what the user can do next.
Avoid blame and implementation detail.
do: Keep the message near the affected context.
Use alert urgency sparingly.
avoid: Using a toast for a blocking validation error.
Replacing a useful error with a generic failure message.

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: Confirms a non-blocking result or offers a short-lived recovery action without interrupting the current task.
components.keyboard: If actionable, the action and dismiss controls are keyboard reachable; auto-dismiss must not remove a focused control.
components.semantics: Use a status announcement for confirmation and a clear action for recovery; do not use a toast for required decisions.
components.accessibility: Announce concise status text without stealing focus; keep actionable content available until it is no longer needed.
content: Confirm the result in plain language.
Make undo or recovery the action label.
do: Use for completed, non-blocking actions.
Allow enough time to read and act.
avoid: Important errors that disappear before recovery.
Stacking so many messages that the user cannot parse them.

components.name: Progress
components.purpose: Shows measurable progress or ongoing activity while the system works.
components.keyboard: Not interactive. If the operation can be stopped or paused, pair it with a labeled action.
components.semantics: Use progressbar semantics for measurable progress and status semantics for indeterminate activity.
components.accessibility: Expose current value, total, label, and completion or error state when known; do not communicate activity only through animation.
content: Name the operation.
Use a meaningful completion statement.
Explain when progress cannot be estimated.
do: Keep the operation label stable.
Provide a cancellation or recovery action when supported.
avoid: A fake percentage that does not reflect work.
Indefinite motion with no status or timeout path.

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: Preserves the expected shape of content while a short-lived load is resolving.
components.keyboard: Not interactive; content is not focusable until it is available.
components.semantics: Expose a loading status when waiting is material; do not expose decorative skeleton shapes as content.
components.accessibility: Avoid creating a focusable phantom layout; provide an error or retry state if loading does not resolve.
content: Use only where the eventual structure is predictable.
Pair long waits with a meaningful status.
do: Use for local, bounded loading.
Preserve layout stability when content arrives.
avoid: Skeletons for unknown or highly dynamic content.
Animation that communicates nothing and never resolves.

components.name: Dialog
components.purpose: Requests focused input or confirmation without losing the current task context.
components.keyboard: On open, focus moves to a sensible first control; Tab stays within the dialog; Escape closes when safe; close returns focus to the trigger.
components.semantics: Use a dialog with a visible title and clear relationship to its trigger; use alertdialog only when immediate attention is required.
components.accessibility: Expose title, description, modal state, busy state, validation, and a labeled close action.
content: Title the decision or task.
Keep the dialog focused on one outcome.
Name the consequence of the primary action.
do: Use for focused decisions or bounded forms.
Preserve entered values when validation fails.
avoid: Long workflows that need persistent navigation.
Closing on outside click when it risks data loss.

components.name: Drawer
components.purpose: Provides contextual detail or secondary controls while keeping the primary surface visible.
components.keyboard: Focus enters the drawer on open, remains contained while open, closes with Escape when safe, and returns to the invoking control.
components.semantics: Use a labeled complementary or dialog surface according to whether the main task remains operable underneath.
components.accessibility: Expose title, relationship to the invoking item, close action, and whether background content is inert.
content: Lead with the context being inspected.
Keep secondary controls grouped and named.
do: Use for inspect-and-return flows.
Keep a clear route back to the source item.
avoid: Hiding required workflow steps in a narrow drawer.
Allowing background controls to steal focus.

components.name: Popover
components.purpose: Shows compact, contextual information or controls near the invoking element.
components.keyboard: Opens from the invoking control; supports Tab within interactive content; Escape closes and returns focus; remains usable when repositioned.
components.semantics: Use a popover for contextual content, not for essential information that must be discovered without the trigger.
components.accessibility: Expose the relationship to the trigger and a labeled close path when the content is interactive.
content: Keep content concise and contextual.
Use a title when the content has more than one control.
do: Anchor to the element that explains the content.
Preserve access when the viewport is constrained.
avoid: Tooltips that contain actions.
Essential instructions available only on hover.

components.name: Tabs
components.purpose: Switches between peer views that share the same context and are useful to compare.
components.keyboard: Tab enters the active tab; Arrow keys move between tabs; activation follows the chosen manual or automatic contract and is consistent.
components.semantics: Use tablist, tab, and tabpanel relationships with stable labels and selected state.
components.accessibility: Expose selected tab, panel relationship, disabled state, and loading state; do not hide the active panel from assistive technology.
content: Use short, parallel labels.
Order tabs by user task or natural sequence.
do: Use for peer views in one context.
Preserve selection when the content refreshes.
avoid: Tabs that are actually navigation between unrelated destinations.
More tabs than a user can scan and compare.

components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.purpose: Shows the user's location in a hierarchy and provides a short route back to parent contexts.
components.keyboard: Links are reachable in document order with Tab and activate with Enter; collapsed ancestors have an explicit control and accessible name.
components.semantics: Use navigation landmarks and mark the current page or location.
components.accessibility: Expose the hierarchy in a readable order; separators are decorative and not announced as content.
content: Use the product's user-facing names.
Keep the current location visible even when ancestors collapse.
do: Use when hierarchy helps orientation.
Keep the trail short enough to scan.
avoid: Repeating the page title without adding location context.
Using internal identifiers as labels.

components.name: Pagination
components.purpose: Moves through a known, bounded set of result pages while preserving position and query context.
components.keyboard: Controls are reachable with Tab and activate with Enter or Space; current page is exposed and previous/next controls are disabled at boundaries.
components.semantics: Use navigation semantics and label the pagination region; do not make page numbers the only way to move.
components.accessibility: Expose current page, total when known, and result updates without moving focus unexpectedly.
content: Name previous and next actions.
Show enough context to understand position.
do: Preserve filters and sort state across pages.
Return focus to the results when new content loads.
avoid: Resetting the user's query on page change.
Infinite scrolling when a bounded result set is easier to orient in.

components.name: Data table
components.purpose: Supports comparison, scanning, sorting, filtering, and selection across structured records.
components.keyboard: Header actions, row actions, selection controls, and pagination are keyboard reachable; horizontal overflow does not hide the active control.
components.semantics: Use native table semantics when relationships are tabular; provide an alternate structure when the layout is not truly tabular.
components.accessibility: Expose column and row headers, sort direction, selection state, and result updates; do not encode status in color alone.
content: Use concise, comparable column labels.
Keep units and date formats consistent.
Explain empty, filtered, and failed states.
do: Keep the most decision-relevant columns visible.
Make row and bulk actions explicit.
avoid: Truncation that prevents identification.
A table that becomes an unstructured card list without a clear mobile contract.

components.name: Tree
components.purpose: Explores hierarchical content with explicit expand, collapse, selection, and loading behavior.
components.keyboard: Arrow keys navigate hierarchy; Right expands, Left collapses, Up and Down move among visible nodes; Home and End reach the bounds.
components.semantics: Use tree semantics only for a hierarchy; use a list or navigation region for a flat set of links.
components.accessibility: Expose level, expanded state, selection, loading, and unavailable child content.
content: Use stable, human-readable node names.
Tell users when a node has children but they are not loaded.
do: Preserve expansion while content refreshes.
Keep selection separate from expansion.
avoid: Requiring pointer precision for expansion.
Moving focus to the root after every update.

components.name: Timeline
components.purpose: Shows ordered events, progress, or history with clear dates, actors, and outcomes where those facts are available.
components.keyboard: Expandable event details are keyboard reachable; chronological order remains understandable without visual connectors.
components.semantics: Use an ordered list or time elements for chronology; interactive details use their native semantics.
components.accessibility: Expose event order, date, label, and expanded state; visual linework is supplementary.
content: Lead with the event and outcome.
Use absolute dates when relative time could mislead.
Distinguish planned, active, and completed events in text.
do: Keep the ordering rule explicit.
Offer a compact and expanded reading path.
avoid: Implying causality solely through proximity.
Filling gaps with invented events or actors.

components.name: Card
components.purpose: Groups a coherent piece of content or task with a clear hierarchy and optional action.
components.keyboard: If the card is actionable, it has one clear focus target or clearly named internal actions; keyboard order follows reading order.
components.semantics: Use a section, article, or link according to the content; do not make a generic container interactive without semantics.
components.accessibility: Expose heading hierarchy and action names; hover styling is never the only indication of interactivity.
content: Give each card one clear subject.
Lead with the information needed to decide what to do next.
do: Use consistent internal hierarchy across a collection.
Make the whole card clickable only when that improves predictability.
avoid: Nested interactive controls inside a single clickable card without a deliberate focus model.
Cards that are only decorative boxes.

components.name: Empty state
components.purpose: Explains why a surface has no content and gives the user a relevant next step.
components.keyboard: The primary recovery or setup action is keyboard reachable and follows the explanation in reading order.
components.semantics: Use a named section or status region; do not treat absence of records as an error without evidence.
components.accessibility: Expose the reason, current scope, and recovery action as text; decorative imagery is optional.
content: Say whether the state is first use, no matches, or unavailable.
Offer one relevant next action.
Do not imply failure when the state is expected.
do: Match the message to the user's current query or scope.
Preserve the user's filters when explaining no matches.
avoid: Generic messages such as Nothing here without context.
Inventing sample data that looks real.

components.name: Prompt composer
components.purpose: Collects an AI request with visible scope, optional attachments or context, and a reversible submit path.
components.keyboard: Supports normal text editing and an explicit submit shortcut; the shortcut is discoverable and does not prevent multiline entry; Escape can stop or dismiss only when the contract says so.
components.semantics: Use a labeled form or textbox with explicit submit, stop, attachment, and scope controls.
components.accessibility: Expose scope, attached context, busy state, errors, and stop action; never imply that an answer is authoritative by visual styling alone.
content: State what the assistant can do in this context.
Show the active scope before submit.
Name privacy or data boundaries when they affect the request.
do: Keep submitted prompts and active scope inspectable.
Allow cancellation when generation is in progress.
avoid: A single unlabeled input that hides context or tool use.
Representing generated output as a silent replacement for user content.

components.name: AI response
components.purpose: Presents generated content with visible lifecycle, provenance affordances, and a clear distinction between suggestion and confirmed fact.
components.keyboard: Response actions, source links, expanders, and retry controls are keyboard reachable; streaming does not repeatedly steal focus.
components.semantics: Use a labeled article or region with status updates separate from the response body; preserve headings and lists in generated content.
components.accessibility: Expose generation state, incomplete or failed status, source availability, and action outcomes; do not rely on animation to show activity.
content: Label generated content as generated.
Separate answer, assumptions, sources, and suggested actions.
State uncertainty when it matters.
do: Keep partial output recoverable.
Make copy, retry, stop, and feedback actions explicit.
avoid: Presenting a guess with the visual authority of a confirmed record.
Hiding tool use, source status, or failure behind a spinner.

components.name: Source list
components.purpose: Shows the sources or context used for a generated answer, including unavailable or partial source evidence.
components.keyboard: The source disclosure and each source link are keyboard reachable; expanding does not move focus unexpectedly.
components.semantics: Use a labeled disclosure or list with links to the source context when links are available.
components.accessibility: Expose source title, type, date when known, unavailable state, and relationship to the generated content.
content: Use source names users can recognize.
Distinguish cited, related, and unavailable sources.
Do not invent a source label when provenance is missing.
do: Keep source context near the claim it supports when possible.
Show when the list is incomplete.
avoid: Citation numbers with no route to source context.
Treating retrieval metadata as proof of correctness.

components.name: AI change review
components.purpose: Lets a user inspect, accept, reject, or undo a generated change before it becomes authoritative.
components.keyboard: Changed regions and accept/reject controls are keyboard reachable; focus moves to the next unresolved change only by an explicit, predictable rule.
components.semantics: Use a diff or structured review pattern with clear old and proposed values; do not overwrite the source silently.
components.accessibility: Expose change location, old value, proposed value, status, and action outcome in text; color highlighting is supplementary.
content: Name the field or record being changed.
Show the proposed value and what it replaces.
Explain conflicts and irreversible effects.
do: Keep the original value inspectable.
Provide undo or a clear recovery path when technically possible.
avoid: Auto-applying a material change without an explicit boundary.
Hiding rejected or conflicted changes from the review history.

components.name: AI operation status
components.purpose: Makes a longer-running assistant or tool operation inspectable, stoppable, and honest about its current result.
components.keyboard: Stop, pause, retry, and details controls are keyboard reachable; completion does not force navigation away from the current task.
components.semantics: Use a labeled status region or task record with explicit lifecycle state and actions.
components.accessibility: Announce meaningful transitions without flooding the user; expose failure reason, retry conditions, and whether output is partial.
content: Name the operation and active scope.
State what is happening now.
State what the user can do if it fails or stalls.
do: Keep operation history inspectable.
Make stop behavior explicit and honest.
avoid: A spinner with no operation name or timeout path.
Reporting completion before the result is available or verified.
